artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Live In Chicago 1990" by Jesus Jones captures the British electronic rock band at a pivotal moment in their early career, performing live during their 1990 tour in support of their debut album, "Liquidizer." The recording showcases their signature fusion of electronic beats, guitar-driven rock, and energetic stage presence, highlighting tracks like "Right Here Right Now," "Real Real Real," "Move Mountains," "Info Freako," and "Never Enough." The album exemplifies the band's ability to blend danceable rhythms with rock intensity, reflecting the emerging alternative electronic sound of the era.

Released originally in 1990 on Demon Records and RT Industries, "Live In Chicago 1990" stands as a testament to Jesus Jones' dynamic live performances and their role in bridging the gap between indie rock and electronic music in the UK scene. While not a commercial release in the traditional sense at the time—initially circulated as a limited live recording—the album has since gained cult status among fans for its raw energy and historical significance. It documents the band's formative years, just before their international breakthrough, and remains a valued document of their early sound and stagecraft.
